solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bet on 'A' team reserve

parts.note: to lay is to bet, as a bookmaker lays odds
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A punter backs the first team while setting the reserves aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bet' looks like a verb about gambling but gives LAY, the bookmaker's word for taking a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something by for later use is to keep it in reserve; the phrase is a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, this place in town?

definitions.meaning: a stuffy, conventional person is called this, slang for unhip
an open public plaza in a town, such as Trafalgar's

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dated spot in town fits the description.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for conventional or unfashionable, and also names an open plaza in a town.

clue.text: One-piece garment bound to fit

parts.note: to bound is to leap or jump
to suit is to fit or be right for someone

explanation.surface: An all-in-one outfit is sure to fit the wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to fit' reads as 'certain to fit', but 'bound' is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an all-in-one outfit covering torso and legs, a single garment.

clue.text: Son tossed in fountain for a joke

indicators.note: tossed in says the son is thrown into the middle of the fountain

parts.note: a jet is a spout of water as from a fountain

explanation.surface: A boy is thrown into a fountain as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a light remark meant to amuse, a synonym for a joke.

clue.text: Chap, old, playing popular instrument

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of old are moved about in play

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: An old fellow is playing a well-loved instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stringed instrument of the lute family, plucked with a plectrum.

clue.text: Awkward? Cane boy's bottom

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: the boy's bottom is the last letter of the word boy in this down clue

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster of old canes a boy's backside, an awkward scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is a difficult or tricky one, so the word means awkward.

clue.text: Mountain goat from heart of Tibet, and last of lynx

indicators.note: the heart of a word is everything inside its first and last letters
last of picks the final letter of the word lynx

explanation.surface: A goat seen in the middle of Tibet alongside a lynx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' here takes all three inner letters of Tibet, IBE, not just the single central one.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat with long curved horns living in high mountains.

clue.text: Nothing unloaded from heavily ornamented sailing ship

indicators.note: unloaded from says the nothing is taken off the ornate word

parts.note: baroque describes a richly decorated style
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is offloaded from an ornate sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing vessel with three or more masts, so it is a type of sailing ship.

clue.text: Posted home, the Spanish guard

parts.note: posted a letter means sent it
in means at home
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish guard is posted back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' suggests a sentry's post, but gives SENT as in mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or watchman keeping guard.

clue.text: Silence leader in Africa, slightly crazy

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Silencing an African leader would be a little mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for senile or a bit dotty, so slightly crazy.

clue.text: Wood stored in cloakroom

indicators.note: stored in says the answer is kept inside the word cloakroom

explanation.surface: Timber has been put away in the cloakroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak is the hard timber of the oak tree, a common wood.

clue.text: Sink crossing turbulent weir that forms a barrier

indicators.note: crossing says the sink stretches over the churned weir, enclosing it

parts.note: to sink is to fall

indicators.note: turbulent water churns, so the letters of weir are churned up

explanation.surface: A basin goes over a rough weir to make a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like a kitchen basin but is the verb meaning drop; 'crossing' wraps it round the 'turbulent' weir.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-resistant wall, or in computing a security system, acts as a barrier.

clue.text: Wild cat, lithe and muscular

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of cat and lithe running loose in new order

explanation.surface: A wild cat is lean and powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic build is strong and fit, so the word means well muscled.

clue.text: French fellow, OK penning verse?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the verse goes inside

parts.note: yes is a way of saying OK

explanation.surface: A Frenchman agrees to write some poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French man's name, as in Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: A duke boarding flight for a lark

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the duke is taken aboard the flight

parts.note: flight means running away, an escape

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes a flight just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring adventure or prank, a lark in the sense of a bit of fun.

clue.text: Ardour shown during craze, a lot

indicators.note: shown during says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm is on display during a passing fad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate enthusiasm, which is what zeal also means.

clue.text: Miss one ahead of time and give way to violent anger

indicators.note: ahead of says the one comes before time in the down entry

parts.note: to miss a train is to ...
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Missing something just before a deadline makes someone fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper or composure completely.

clue.text: Choose with great care labourer with rock-breaking tool

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
a pick is a pointed tool for breaking rock

explanation.surface: A worker carefully selects a tool for breaking stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To select individually by hand implies careful, personal selection.

clue.text: Liberal accepted by association, up to a point

indicators.note: accepted by says the Liberal is taken inside the association

parts.note: a party is a political association

explanation.surface: A Liberal is admitted to a group, though only to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only in part holds to a limited degree, up to a point.

clue.text: Bird of the poultry kind — not female bird

indicators.note: not says the female letter is left out of the poultry bird

parts.note: a fowl is a domestic bird kept for eggs or meat

explanation.surface: A bird resembling poultry, but not the hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' at the start is part of the wordplay; the definition is the final 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, so simply a bird.

clue.text: A short cut in neighbourhood

indicators.note: short says the word for cut loses its last letter

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop

explanation.surface: A shortcut through the local district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' reads as one phrase, but 'short' trims REAP to REA.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or locality, much like a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Plucky in match

definitions.meaning: brave, willing to have a go
a contest or fixture in sport

explanation.surface: A brave performer in a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means willing and brave, and also a contest such as a football match.

clue.text: Ready to complain once head of government's left

indicators.note: has left says the leading letter goes away from the word for complain

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: People are ready to grumble once the prime minister has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe fruit is ready to eat, so the word means ready.

clue.text: Beverage teenager brewed

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters of teenager stewed into a new mix

explanation.surface: A youngster makes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This unfermented Chinese tea is a drink, so a beverage.

clue.text: A boy enthralled by my illness

indicators.note: enthralled by says the boy is held captive inside my

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone confesses their illness has captivated a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is a disease or ailment, so an illness.

clue.text: Page item, tiny piece

parts.note: an article is an item, as in an article of clothing

explanation.surface: A page lists an item as a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute portion or fragment of matter.
